questions.question_text: One of the following statements for adenyl cyclase is wrong. Identify.

options.D: Active only when associated with G Protein

questions.explanation: Phosphodiesterase degrades cAMP, whereas adenyl cyclase synthesizes it; it is not inactivated by phosphodiesterase.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following device is used to increase the efficiency of drug delivery via aerosols?
questions.explanation: Tube spacers are used with metered-dose inhalers to reduce oral deposition and increase pulmonary drug delivery efficiency.

questions.question_text: One of the uses given below for opioids is not correct. Indicate
questions.explanation: Opioids are well known as analgesics, antitussives, and antidiarrhoeals, but they lack significant anti-inflammatory activity.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is used as a preservative in ophthalmic preparations?
questions.explanation: Benzalkonium chloride is the most widely used antimicrobial preservative in ophthalmic formulations.

questions.question_text: The activity of the following drugs is dependent on Pheny-N-alkyl one piperidine moiety?
questions.explanation: Meperidine possesses a 1-methyl-4-phenylpiperidine structural core essential for its opioid activity.

questions.question_text: One of the organism mentioned below is used as a biological indicator in I.P. for ethylene oxide sterilization. Choose the correct one.
questions.explanation: Bacillus subtilis spores are conventionally used as biological indicators to monitor ethylene oxide sterilization processes.

questions.question_text: The most common causative agent of Bacterial Pneumonia is:
questions.explanation: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the leading bacterial cause of community-acquired pneumonia.

questions.question_text: Creatinine clearance is used as a measurement for
questions.explanation: Creatinine clearance closely approximates the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of the kidneys.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct starting material for the synthesis of Ethacrynic Acid
questions.explanation: Ethacrynic acid synthesis classically starts with 2,3-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid derivatives.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct metabolic process for Phenobarbitone
questions.explanation: Phenobarbital is metabolized primarily via aromatic hydroxylation (p-hydroxylation) followed by conjugation with glucuronic acid.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following antihistaminic is a basic ether?
questions.explanation: Diphenhydramine is an ethanolamine derivative containing a basic ether linkage.

questions.question_text: Conductivity cells are made up of
questions.explanation: Standard conductivity cells use two parallel sheets or electrodes of platinum coated with platinum black.

questions.question_text: The chemical shift value is

options.C: Ratio of the number of Protons in each group
options.D: Proportional to the total number of protons

questions.explanation: Chemical shift values (in ppm) are independent of the applied magnetic field strength.

questions.question_text: Select the equation that gives the rate of drug dissolution from a tablet
questions.explanation: The Noyes-Whitney equation describes the rate of dissolution of solid pharmaceuticals.

questions.question_text: Energy absorbed in U.V. region produces changes in

options.A: The rotational energy of the molecule
options.B: The vibrational energy of the molecule
options.C: The electronic energy of the molecule
options.D: All the three energy levels of the molecule

questions.explanation: Ultraviolet and visible light absorption promote electronic transitions within molecules.

questions.question_text: Dose dumping is a problem in the formulation of
questions.explanation: Dose dumping refers to the accidental, rapid release of a drug from a controlled-release formulation.

questions.question_text: The initial distribution of a drug into the tissue is determined chiefly by

options.A: Rate of blood flow to the tissue
options.B: Plasma protein binding of the drug

questions.explanation: Initial distribution phase is primarily perfusion-limited, depending on regional blood flow.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct characteristic of the epidermal cells and cuticle of Atropa belladonna leaf

options.C: Algal cell walls with smooth cuticle

questions.explanation: Atropa belladonna leaf epidermis typically shows wavy anticlinal walls and a striated cuticle.

questions.question_text: Meclizine hydrochloride is prepared from which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Meclizine is synthesized by alkylating 1-(4-chlorobenzhydryl)piperazine with 3-methylbenzyl chloride or 3-methylbenzaldehyde.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an Ex-Officio member of the State Pharmacy Council?

options.B: Chief Administrative Medical Officer of the state

questions.explanation: The Chief Medical Officer of the State typically serves as an ex-officio member of the State Pharmacy Council under pharmacy regulations.

questions.question_text: Phloroglucinol and Hydrochloric acid produces pink or red colour with
questions.explanation: Phloroglucinol and HCl (Wiesner test) react with lignin to produce a pink or red color.

questions.question_text: One of the forms mentioned below is used to issue licence for wholesale of drugs other than specified in schedule C, C_1 and X. Choose the correct one.
questions.explanation: Form 21B is utilized for issuing wholesale licenses for drugs other than those specified in schedules C, C1, and X.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct chemical name for Chloropromazine hydrochloride
questions.explanation: Chlorpromazine is 2-chloro-10-[3-(dimethylamino)propyl]phenothiazine hydrochloride, corresponding to position 3 or 2 depending on numbering conventions; D is the standard accepted IUPAC nomenclature choice.

questions.question_text: Wavelength of a radiation is $5.0 \mu$. Wave number corresponding to that is:
questions.explanation: Wave number $\bar{\nu} = 1 / \lambda = 1 / (5.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ cm}) = 2000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$? Wait, calculation: $1 / 5\mu m = 1 / (5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ cm}) = 2000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$. Let's check option B: $2000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.question_text: Choose the synthetic adrenocortical steroid, which do not occur in nature.
questions.explanation: The 1,4-diene structure corresponds to Prednisolone, a synthetic corticosteroid.
